record.paper_title: Ductile-to-brittle transition and yielding in soft amorphous materials: perspectives and open questions
record.original_question: How general is the criterion that transient shear bands form during shear startup when a stress overshoot occurs, given its assumptions about the number of mechanical variables, sensitivity to constitutive models and viscosity ratios, and experimental complications such as wall slip?

evidence.quote: However, the startup criterion (i, above) was derived within some caveats [93–95] – most notably assuming only two interacting mechanical variables (the shear stress and one component of normal stress or one fluidity variable, for example) – and Ref. 95 indeed confirmed it to hold in some models of polymeric fluids, but not others.
Taken together, these works suggest that the evidence for shear banding associated with startup stress overshoot is quite widespread, 94 but that further work is needed concerning its generality .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a homogeneous, incompressible, viscoelastic complex fluid subjected to simple shear startup: at time t = 0 a constant shear rate γ̇ is imposed on a fluid initially at rest, and one records the time-dependent shear stress σ(t,γ̇) together with the velocity profile v_x(y,t) across the gap. Within a class of one-dimensional continuum constitutive models for such a fluid, an analytical linear-stability criterion has been derived predicting that transient inhomogeneous flow (a transient shear band in v_x(y,t)) appears during shear startup whenever the macroscopic shear-stress response σ(t) exhibits a stress overshoot, i.e. whenever ∂σ/∂t changes sign from positive to negative at some finite time. This criterion was obtained under the simplifying assumption that the constitutive dynamics involves only two coupled mechanical variables (for instance the shear stress together with one normal-stress component, or the shear stress together with a single scalar fluidity variable).

Investigate the generality of this "stress-overshoot ⇒ transient shear banding during startup" criterion. Specifically:

(a) Determine whether the criterion extends to constitutive models with more than two coupled dynamical variables (for example, tensorial polymer-conformation models such as Giesekus, Rolie-Poly with chain stretch, or multi-mode models), and identify model classes for which the implication fails.

(b) Characterize the sensitivity of the criterion to the choice of constitutive model and to the solvent-to-polymer (or background-to-structural) viscosity ratio η_s/η_p, identifying the parameter regimes in which transient banding does or does not accompany a stress overshoot.

(c) Determine the conditions, if any, under which experimental complications such as wall slip at the rheometer boundaries can be rigorously separated from genuine bulk transient shear banding triggered by stress overshoot, and whether the criterion can be made into a sharp necessary and/or sufficient condition once such effects are accounted for.

Provide either a proof of the criterion's validity under explicit, broadly applicable hypotheses, or counterexamples delineating its precise domain of validity.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent simulations and analyses indicate the startup stress-overshoot criterion for transient shear banding holds for some constitutive models (e.g. Rolie-Poly without stretch, Johnson–Segalman) but fails or is unclear in others (e.g. Giesekus), and is sensitive to the number of dynamical variables, viscosity ratios, and possible wall slip. The general validity of the criterion remains an active open question, with calls in the literature for further theoretical and experimental work.

status_evidence.title: Transient shear banding during startup flow: Insights from nonlinear simulations
status_evidence.snippet: Transient shear banding may be absent in some cases despite stress overshoot during startup, regardless of whether the startup shear rate is in monotonic or nonmonotonic regions of the constitutive curve.
status_evidence.claim: Stress overshoot is not sufficient for transient shear banding in all constitutive models, indicating the criterion's generality is limited.

status_evidence.title: Triggers and signatures of shear banding in steady and time-dependent flows
status_evidence.snippet: A theoretical criterion was derived assuming two dynamical viscoelastic variables; its general status is not completely clear and it appears not to apply straightforwardly in the Giesekus model.
status_evidence.claim: The criterion was derived under a two-variable assumption and is known to fail or be unclear in some polymer models.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of startup shear flow data of linear polystyrene blends
status_evidence.snippet: Recent experimental analysis examines whether shear stress features in startup are caused by transient shear banding, indicating the question remains under active investigation.
status_evidence.claim: The link between startup stress features and transient shear banding is still being experimentally investigated.
